Second endpoint: Grade 1 (coordinate rank 1), Term 1, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics', Sub-strand 'Emergent reading skills (taught in Shared and Group Guided Reading lessons)' - 'Interprets pictures to make up own story, that is, \'reads\' the pictures'. The two statements express the same emergent capability of constructing an own narrative from pictures; 'interprets pictures' paraphrases rather than extends 'makes up own story by \'reading\' the pictures'. There is no evidence of expanded capability (no longer or more complex texts, no wider letter/word demand, no greater independence), and both endpoints carry exactly one identical Learning Component (57dd23e1) whose description is verbatim the Grade 1 statement, with LC tag, LC text and shared-component overlap at jaccard 1.0 - the signature of CAPS's deliberate cross-grade repetition rather than developmental extension. Grade-rank order alone, the shared sub-strand label, and the shared Learning Component cannot license buildsTowards. The recurrence is nonetheless pair-specific and instructionally coherent: the same named 'Emergent reading skills' sub-strand carries picture-based meaning making across the Grade R to Grade 1 transition, which is meaningful reinforcement without demonstrated dependency, so symmetric relatesTo with null direction and unchanged canonical endpoint order is the complete judgment. Material limitation: each endpoint omits 24 source-evidence items and has truncated LC metadata, and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context (including merged Grade and Term banner nodes), so a fuller source could alter this reading; confidence is moderated accordingly.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade 3 (rank 3) Skills. The first, 'Reads own writing to a friend or a group', sits under Term 2 > WRITING > Shared, Group and Independent Writing; the second, "Reads own and others' writing", sits under Term 3 > READING AND PHONICS > Paired/Independent Reading. Within the same grade the direction Term 2 to Term 3 is permitted, and the change is substantive rather than mere repeated wording: the learner moves from reading back only their own composed text aloud to a friend or group, to reading both their own and peers' written texts in paired/independent reading, which broadens the text source beyond self-authored material and shifts the activity into the independent reading context. Fluency and confidence in reading one's own writing aloud plausibly supports success in decoding and comprehending peers' unfamiliar handwritten texts, so buildsTowards first_to_second is supported. Evidence is bounded: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and LC evidence for the second endpoint is truncated, so confidence is moderate.

Symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the correct complete judgment; canonical endpoint order is preserved and is not semantic.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 1 (rank 1) Writing / 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' skills aimed at producing texts for the classroom reading corner, but the identity scopes differ by term: the first is Term 1 ('Contributes ideas in Shared Writing for a class story recorded by the teacher on charts'), the second is Term 2 ('Writes and illustrates a caption or short sentence on a topic to contribute to a book for the reading corner'). Experience generating and shaping ideas for shared class texts supports success in composing one's own caption, so buildsTowards runs Term 1 to Term 2 (first_to_second), which is a permitted within-grade forward direction. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), but the retained statement text and identity-scope terms are sufficient and consistent.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Reading, the first under Term 1 (Emergent reading skills) and the second under Term 2 (Emergent reading), so the only permitted developmental direction within the grade is earlier Term 1 to later Term 2. The Term 1 statement establishes controlled left-to-right eye movement/visual tracking (LC tags 'eye movements', 'left to right', 'tracking'); the Term 2 statement applies tracking to actual print and meaning-making, pointing to words when 'reading' (LC tags 'pointing', 'tracking', 'words') and using pictures to predict the story while distinguishing pictures from words. This is a substantive extension from non-print ocular tracking to directional print tracking plus emergent comprehension, so proficiency in the Term 1 skill supports success in the Term 2 skill rather than being mere repeated wording (lexical overlap is negligible, jaccard 0.02). judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade 3 (rank 3), Term 2, Listening and Speaking (Oral) Skills from the same printed table row, but under different Sub-strands ('Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities' vs 'Daily / Weekly activities in all areas of Language and other subjects'). Their content differs materially: participating in group/class discussions, suggesting topics and contributing ideas (LCs: contributes ideas in discussions, suggests topics for discussion, participates in group and class discussions) versus listening and responding to radio or intercom announcements and instructions (LCs: listens to / responds to announcements and instructions). These are complementary oral-language competences within the same term — receptive listening with an appropriate spoken response, and interactive contribution to discussion — so there is substantive coherence in oral listening-and-responding, but no evidence that proficiency in one supports success in the other, and no term or grade separation to ground a developmental direction (same Grade 3, same Term 2). Textual overlap is negligible (only 'and'), so shared Skill Area, page and rank alone would not justify buildsTowards. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each) and all supplied nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, including merged Grade and Term banner nodes; this bounds but does not contradict the judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 (rank 3) Shared Reading Skills under Reading and Phonics: the first is Term 4 'Uses a dictionary to find new vocabulary and their meanings'; the second is Term 3 'Reads a range of different types of poems around a topic and discusses these (both form and meanings, word selection)'. They cohere substantively around attention to word meanings and word choice in shared reading, and the dictionary skill is a plausible complement to discussing poem vocabulary and meanings. However, the evidence shows no dependency: dictionary reference skill and poem reading/discussion are distinct capabilities, and the shared tokens ('meanings', 'a', 'and') plus a single shared LC tag ('reading') are largely generic rather than demonstrating expanded capability of one from the other. A Term 4 to Term 3 developmental direction within the same grade is in any case invalid, and the available Term 3 to Term 4 evidence is too thin to assert buildsTowards, so symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), limiting fuller comparison.
